utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Harvey can introduce his colleague first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is your microphone activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Testing, testing. Yes, now I hear me. As I was trying to say. With me is Juan Pablo Perez-Leon Acevedo from Peru who has been assisting my team since June and will be here until at least December. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, I'm terribly impressed with your ability to pronounce a long and distinguished and complicated name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It still is only one person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, without trying to play master of ceremonies, I think Ms. Sutherland had to indicate to the Trial Chamber her position with respect to the annexes that have been temporarily made confidential, so perhaps we could do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Your Honours, the application that was made at the 11th hour the other evening when we received the filings was for the annexes to be -- remain confidential because they contain certain information. And Your Honours made that provisional ruling. I stated that it was because there was the address of the witness and also for security concerns. In fact, I should have gone wider and said for privacy issues as well but in dealing with it in haste I didn't say that. Mr. Robinson and I have had a discussion before court this morning and it may be that we can agree who can be redacted from the appendices and we would ask that we can get back to the Court on next Monday if we are not in agreement. We would deal with it over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's very much appreciated. And in the meantime, the -- on a related matter, the Prosecution's request for leave to -- for the extension of word limit is granted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, finally back to me, Mr. President. I would like to make a motion for a leave to reply orally to the -- to the Prosecution's response to our motion for the ninth suspension of proceedings which I would think that you might be minded to decide today since we asked that the proceedings be suspended as of Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it related to KDZ-456?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the decision is now being filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Then you don't need to hear my reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, just in relation to the matter I was addressing you on, one of the documents that's subject to that is listed on Mr. Karadzic's list of documents to be used in cross-examination with the next witness -- with this current witness. And so if he was wanting to use that document, then I'd suggest that we would need to go into private session to deal with that issue since Mr. Robinson and I won't have resolved the issue before Mr. Karadzic completes his cross-examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that Mr. Robinson will advise his client accordingly. Yes, let's bring in the witness. While we are waiting for the witness being brought in, Mr. Karadzic, the -- I note that the Prosecution has spent for its examination-in-chief two and a half hours. Although we granted you the five hours, provided that he's admitted pursuant to Rule 92 ter, the evidence of which consists of 734 pages, but now that he testified viva voce and the time the Prosecution spent only two and a half hours and that the -- we didn't admit as many associated exhibits as expected, now we -- the Chamber is of the view you should be able to finish in less than three hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may say, considering that the OTP touched on political subjects through this witness which is probably necessary because he was among the top officials of the SDA party and he was a Member of Parliament, I will probably need a bit more time. So I kindly ask you to take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's why we are giving you a little bit more time than the time the Prosecution has spent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you have three hours, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, that would leave, I think, 15 minutes before the end of the day to start the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm just thinking for scheduling purposes if we're not going to get to the next witness today then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes -- no --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Because Mr. Tieger may have some re-examination and I'm just thinking if it's sensible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And also the Chamber is minded -- rise 15 minutes earlier than usual today. So it's apparent that we'll not --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Start the next witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How are you, Mr. Sejmenovic? Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for asking. I'm fine. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Today you will be asked by Mr. Radovan Karadzic in his cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sejmenovic.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have three hours at our disposal, though I was hoping that we would continue on Monday. In order for us not to request that, I will ask you whenever possible, and of course I will try to achieve that by asking you simple questions, to answer whenever possible with yes or no with exceptions, of course. I wish to ask you the following. You are a founding member and a member of the Municipal Board of SDA. Were you ever a member of the Main Board of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of the Main Board of the SDA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you attend the founding session of the SDA in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not attend that if you mean the foundation meeting which was held at the Holiday Inn hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, on the 26th of May. But you were a deputy and you said yesterday that you came every time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is to say you were familiar with all the political developments among the top leaders in Bosnia-Herzegovina including the negotiations between the three leaders and so on; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by my position, we could not say that I was familiar with all the political developments and the details of negotiations. From the position that I held, I could know a certain number of details and some relations, both in terms of other parties, relations with other parties, and negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is quite all right. It is important for me to determine what you were familiar with and what you were not. I have nothing negative or positive to say about that. It's just a matter of determining. I wish to ask you the following: Did you testify before any court in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in which case if you did?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not testified in any case before the court in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I was called so that the court in Travnik would determine certain facts through me in a case that I had nothing to do with, and during the first conversation it was established that I did not have a direct connection with that case so that in the procedural sense I was not involved in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you give any statements in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statements that have to do with the issues dealt with in this court were something I gave to representatives of the United Nations and representatives of this Tribunal which was founded somewhat later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll move to the crisis situation. Up until then, did you receive instructions or directives from the Party of Democratic Action, that is to say from its headquarters, in a written or oral fashion? From what point in time did you have communication with Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, regular and unobstructed communication with Sarajevo was in operation up until the end of January or -- excuse me, up until March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that up until the end of March?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During one part of the month of March. I have to clarify this for the Trial Chamber. Direct communication, direct contact with the party does not only imply the sending of instructions by telephone or written instructions. It also implies that the president of the party would go to the headquarters of the party to attend meetings, and therefore it includes physical communication. The physical communication was already made difficult in late March and in the month of April it was no longer possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you could not even have telephone or fax connections?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the telephone lines were still working but what level of decisions were -- the decisions that were forwarded, it is something I don't know or the form of the decisions, because my position was such that I was not directly involved in this hierarchy. And the contacts with the party leadership were directed to the president of the party in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As for the Deputies Club of deputies from SDA, did it discuss the possible resolution of the crisis in BiH before the war, that is to say the peace plans and everything else that was in the air at the time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably mean the Deputies Club at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite clear to you that each party discussed important issues during the meetings of the deputies clubs, so that included the party that I was a member of. On several occasions at club meetings we discussed various issues that concerned the state, but at which meeting the club discussed which issues that's something I cannot recollect. Either the dates or the precise chronology, but I do know that there was talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now please see 1D04493. Did you agree to have co-operation with the HDZ and the SDS even before elections in terms of dismantling the communist system and creating a post-election coalition?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a general agreement because the SDA declared its main political goal and that was dismantling the one-party communist system. The SDS also declared that that was its main goal, the HDZ also declared the same goal as its main goal. On the basis of this common goal in the pre-election period we already achieved some co-operation. As for the SDA, this co-operation was open, sincere, direct, and the SDS agreed to some elements of this co-operation. And later on it showed in practice that it did not agree with that and that it pursued a different policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to that. Can we please zoom in on the upper hand right corner in B/C/S so that Mr. Sejmenovic could easily read it. Yes, just that. Were these the basic principles and goals of the party, that is to say the affirmation of human rights, democracy, and then under item 3 we see the affirmation of the national identity of the Bosnian Muslims. And further on, if we look at the market economy and everything else that was all the same, common, also the preservation of the territorial integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina and of Yugoslavia and also preserving its borders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I wish to point out to item 4 which you skipped and I think the Chamber should be minded of it and it includes autonomy and freedom of activity for all religious communities. So all religious communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. So was there full agreement between the SDS and the SDA about these principles? Did the SDS accept this programme so that a coalition would be possible, both at the central level because this was the programme at the central level, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, it was similar at the central level. The SDS accepted some elements of the programme. By definition it could not accept everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it did not dispute or reject coalition, which means that this was acceptable for the Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was acceptable for the Serbs. It was acceptable for us at the moment when this list of goals was written and under the circumstances under which it was written and in the Yugoslavia which existed in such a shape at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us have a look at the penultimate paragraph, saying that information meetings were held in Prijedor, Kamicani, Carkovo, Zecovi, Hambarine, Kozarac, Cejreci, Puharska, Rakovcani Biscani, Rizvanovici and other places. These villages which are listed here were all 100 per cent populated by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not 100 per cent populated by Muslims. I wish we would not improvise when we use specific terms. Some of these villages had a mixed up ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I said almost, not that they were really 100 per cent. But were they predominantly Muslim populated villages?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were and the others weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which was the one that did not have a Muslim majority?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Puharska was not populated 100 per cent by Muslims. Rakovcani, Cejreci also. Some of the villages where this was held, Kozarac as well -- or if you wish I can analyse it village by village and provide a bit more specific information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there more than 60, 70, or even 80 per cent of Muslims in terms of the population. Not 100 per cent but much more than one half.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in some villages, and in others not. But if we were to take all the villages together we could say that it was probably 70 or 80 per cent of non-Serbian population. There were other ethnic groups there in addition to Bosniak Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you are noted here as the secretary of this board; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you whether you know -- you had not been born at the time but do you know that in Prijedor the municipality of Prijedor as it was in the 1990s was increased by other municipalities which were joined to it? Would you agree and do you know that Kozarac used to be a municipality and so was Ljubija and some other places as well?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Omarska used to be a municipality as well and I'm familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Omarska with the Serbian majority, Kozarac with Muslim and Ljubija with a Croat majority?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now we can guess, you and I, because we would have to go to archives, see what was the information, and then provide specific answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1821, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Communist authorities changed the statute of the Prijedor municipality before the elections?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what was changed in the Prijedor municipality statute?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at document 1D02908. No, that's not the one. That's not the document. 02908. Did I say that correctly? Yes, now we have it. Please have a look at Article 3 and tell us whether it is correct that Article 42 is changed and that social funds were established, socially owned funds were established. Is it correct that they were meant to be used for sports, culture, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here, that socially owned funds were to be established. What sort of funds they were, I don't know, nor do I know how that had been regulated before this change of statute. I would need to see both the document and a little bit of time to study that and then give an opinion that could be of any use to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further it says that Article 43 is changed and the social funds shall be financed from contributions for the use and other funds in accordance with the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct but it doesn't tell you anything because it's not clear what these funds were and how they would be used. There are no rules about the use of the funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says under Article 3 the new Article 42 will be as follows: [As read] "In order to ensure material and other conditions for the building, use, and protection of residential buildings and activities of special importance for the society on the principles of mutuality and solidarity in accordance with the law socially owned funds shall be established?" So everything is specified, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the purpose of its use is specified under Article 3, that's true. So one could say that these are a sort of communal funds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In addition to the communal funds were there also funds for the youth, for sports, for culture, and other funds?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, joint social activities were mostly financed from funds and that is a clear thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the next page. Can you please focus on this Article 6. You might even read it out aloud, Article 6 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "open" the composition and selection of the council before Article 223 shall be raised and Article 223 shall be changed and read as follows: The Assembly of the municipality of Prijedor will consist of one chamber and it will have 90 deputies of which 41.59 per cent are of Serbian ethnicity, 38.7 per cent of Muslim ethnicity, 6.7 per cent of Croatian nationality, the Yugoslavs shall make up 9.7 per cent and 3.31 per cent of other ethnic groups in relation to the ethnic composition of the population of the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 6 of this document or perhaps 7 -- no, 6 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this article, 13, amends Article 260 of the statute, changing the way the president of the municipality is elected and it introduces a new element that did not exist under the Communist regime, namely, that the president of the municipality will be nominated by the winning party?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the reasons why both you and I wanted to topple the Communist regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before doing that, could you explain to us how this is relevant to your case, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's the basis for all that happened in the elections and after the elections. If you look at Article 1, you will see that the ethnic picture is that 41.5 per cent are Serbs, 37.something are Muslims and 17.something are Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly suggest to the Court that to this we add information that this data reflects a census that was done 20 years prior and a new census was pending just a few months after this document was drafted and indeed this new census was carried out. I just wanted to clarify for the Court what these percentages really mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, very well. We'll mark it for identification as Exhibit D1822, but please bear in mind our time is limited, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us just clear one thing up, Mr. Sejmenovic, are you claiming that in 1981 there was no census and that these are not data from 1981?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that. I don't know the exact date of the census, but you said yourself it was ten years before this document was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the Serb side object to the outcome of the elections and that even the ex-Communists and Serbs complained that the elections were rigged?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at the level of the state or in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prijedor demands were made to the local electoral commission. All complaints were reviewed according to the legal procedure. Some of those complaints were granted and in a minor segment the elections had to be repeated in the presence of observers and quite regularly these elections were repeated, although they could not significantly change the overall outcome of the elections.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D04495.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this. In the top left corner you see your name in Cyrillic. It says you were elected with 812 votes more than the left-wing candidate won, the man called Marko Pavic, who is still mayor of Prijedor, and you got 812 votes more than he. A bit lower you will see that the SDS is unhappy about the ethnic structure, that it does not reflect the census percentages which were 41.6 per cent for Serbs as opposed to 31.7 Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we raise this page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall this document? It's Kozarski Vjesnik, 7 December 1990.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember Kozarski Vjesnik published all sorts of interpretations of the electoral process, but I also remember that the SDS in Prijedor wanted that there should be more Serbs in Prijedor than there really were and it was not our fault that there were not more Serbs as the SDS wished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's not go into that debate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we raise this page. Can we see the bottom part of the left column.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the SDS is complaining that the quotas written into the statute were not observed. The SDS wants the annulment of the elections and the opposition replies that everything is according to the actual ethnic representation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see page 2 in English. Do you remember the question and answer the question, or shall I ask Mr. Karadzic to repeat his question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be good if he could repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see in these texts that the SDS is asking for the elections to be annulled because they suspect there has been falsification because the ethnic quotas are not complied with?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDS lost these elections. That's the main reason why the SDS complained, looking for any excuse whatsoever to organise extraordinary elections. The main reason for these complaints is the SDS did not win in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not investigating now whether this is true or not. I just want to establish one thing: Did the SDS have objections?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you're showing me a page from a local newspaper. I don't know who wrote this article, how they wrote it, with what intentions. But one thing is certain: The SDS complained and protested about the result of the elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's good.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the upper right corner. That's it and we need the first page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This says, doesn't it, that both the communists and the DSS --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There is a whistling sound when Mr. Karadzic speaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. There seems to be a technical problem. I do have the same -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I the only one who doesn't hear it. Should I push the microphone away? Is that better? But I hear myself, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do the interpreters have the same problem?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We will not know until Mr. Karadzic resumes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see, Mr. Sejmenovic, that the SK-SDP and the DSS, that is, both left-wing parties, say that the chairman of the electoral board in Hambarine just gave a present of 500 votes to the SDA and they wrote into the ballot the SDA candidate under number 2 and that's why a demand was made to initiate proceedings. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that. It's written in the article, but what I'm saying is that anyone could write any kind of article. The SDA also had its own view of the electoral process, its own interpretation, but you don't quote those articles. You quote only those that reflected the dissatisfaction of the SDS. The electoral commission took into account all complaints and followed regular procedure in completing the electoral process, as envisaged by the law. There was a need to repeat one part of it and it was repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, we are now not trying to establish whether these people are right or not, but do you agree that this text does not refer to the SDS. It refers to two left-wing parties, the Communists and the Socialists?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says something different at the bottom. The Communists actually thank the doubting Toms for their mistrust, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying something different. The Communists and Socialists said that 500 ballots were allocated by one man to the SDA. That man voted on behalf of 500 local residents. That's not the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the Communist bloc that we all wanted to defeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I also mention to the Court one important detail regarding these articles? These were elections into the house of municipalities. That's a separate electoral list and the voting was for the representative of the Prijedor municipality into the house of municipalities of the republic parliament. There were separate elections for municipal MPs. So this is a different list and I can name the person who voted -- I can say that the person called Mevludin Sejmenovic got the votes of a significant number of Serbs as well and the voting was by name and surname. I can even provide the names of these people who voted for me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we can admit it -- but I'm still struggling to understand the relevance. I don't think you are claiming this is one of the reasons for the arrest of this witness. Let's come to 1992 -- this is all 1990s.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But with all due respect, Your Excellencies, you should say that to the Prosecution, that they should not spread their ambitions to the pre-war and pre-electoral period. My questions emanate from the examination-in-chief and with every witness they repeat the whole story, so I have to challenge every witness on every point. That's what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit it as Defence Exhibit D1823.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that already towards the end of August, throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina there were many hotbeds of crisis and rising tensions and the three of us, Izetbegovic, Kljuic, and myself, made a proposal, or rather, issued an instruction that the SDS and the HDZ should establish joint groups to monitor any incidents and developments that could affect inter-ethnic relations?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of August, as you said, there was a whole series of crises caused by incidents triggered by paramilitary units, by the JNA, and by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have to specify what kind of crises these were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you what I'm asking you. Did we recommend joint groups --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before the discussion goes any further. The previous exhibits related to 1990. There was a suggestion by the Court to go to 1992. Now there's a reference in the abstract to August. Perhaps it's useful to specify whether it's 1990, 1991, or 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot help making an introduction into how the crisis occurred and what we did to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The question was whether it was in 1990 or 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] End August 1991, the beginning of the crisis. The crisis did not begin in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D181, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, I'm not going into whether this was necessary. I'm just reminding you, if you remember, that three leaders of national parties recommended that joint groups should be formed to monitor events that lead to tensions and report back to the head offices?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll be precise, it's the SDA that suggested this initiative to the SDS and the HDZ. The SDS accepted this initiative at the level of the Presidency, and that's how this initiative originated. I believe it is important to mention before this Court who originated this idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see in the second paragraph it says that the groups would inform the leaderships of their parties with all the members of the groups signed and that they will report on all the events and also underline all the differences that may exist between them? Did you actually proceed this way?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We actually did even more than is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We lost the -- if Mr. Karadzic take a look into the transcript whether it reflects all the conversations. Please put a pause between the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last question and answer: [In English] "Did you actually proceed this way? "We actually did even more than is written here."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, previous one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: And that is satisfactory. [Interpretation] The previous question is -- I think it's good and the answer is also good. Right. Everything's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was the answer to the previous question? You started asking the second question while your first question was being interpreted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said "do you see, do you see in the second paragraph," not do you say. Do you see in the second paragraph that the head offices of the parties, not leaderships, should be informed with all members of the groups signed and highlighting all the differences between the members of the groups concerning the incidents -- actually, the mistake in the transcript is that "Did you actually proceed this way?" Is a question, not an answer. And the witness answered: "We actually did even more than is written here." That's the only remedy the transcript requires.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the answer to the previous question was "yes"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can say "yes," but I have already said that we worked in the spirit of inter-ethnic tolerance and we tried to avoid problems even more than is stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification, pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1824, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have an observation, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe that document is already in evidence as D00264.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D04494, could we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirza Mujadzic, after the elections, issued this statement saying that they were pleased with their victory over the left forces, not the SDS, and that the leftist forces nevertheless succeeded and this shows that, yet again, Prijedor turned out to be some kind of mini-Moscow.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the president of the SDA and the presidents of other parties expressed their pleasure in different ways because they had scored a victory over the League of Communists. This is a manifestation of that satisfaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1824, Your Honours -- I'm sorry, Exhibit D1824.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that one of the reasons for this crisis were the police insignia; right? The Serb side thought that they had established the Krajina and that those who are within the AR Krajina should wear new insignia; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've already discussed August 1991. Many things happened from August 1991 until the problem of insignia, that came up in 1992 -- in April, actually. So it was almost a year later. I repeat, chronologically speaking, many things happened between those two dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. I am following the instructions of the Trial Chamber to move on to 1992 as soon as possible, otherwise I wouldn't mind discussing 1991.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be right for us to know that many things happened in the meantime before this happened in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then tell me, when was the Autonomous Region of Krajina established?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first information about the SDS planning the establishment of the Autonomous Region of Krajina came after one month, after that document was signed, the one that you showed, stating that inter-ethnic relations would not be disrupted. Soon after that the SDS started preparing for the establishment of the Serb Autonomous Region and then soon after that the SDS took the repeater on the Kozara.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait. Can you answer this question: When was the Autonomous Region of Krajina established?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second half of 1991. That's when the meeting in Celinac was held. I don't know the exact date. And at that meeting you discussed the establishment of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was established in the first half of September by way of a response to the defeat of the historic Serb-Muslim agreement, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these epic categories like historic agreement this and that and the other thing, could these questions please not be put to me? This is a figment of people's imagination. I would like to deal with specific questions. After a parliamentary debate in Bosnia-Herzegovina, stating that things like this should not be done, this was established in the second half of 1991. I'm not in a position to pin-point the date and the gentleman just said what date that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that July and August of 1991 did not involve intensive talks on an historic agreement between the Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody negotiated with everybody in order to avert a war --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. The question is very specific. Izetbegovic supported the negotiations. The negotiations were proposed and conducted by Zulfikarpasic and Filipovic. Do you know that, these two months in the summer of 1991 were marked by these intensive negotiations; and then on the 31st of August, Mr. Izetbegovic no longer rendered his support to this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The academician Filipovic and Mr. Zulfikarpasic travelled to Belgrade, that I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The details, what they talked about, I don't know about any of these details, and I know least of all what the outcome of these negotiations was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, can this be admitted, what is here, right here? The witness confirmed that the democratic forces were cheering the fact that the Communists had lost.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is not what I said. I said expressing satisfaction, whereas cheering in a certain way is something that means a completely different thing in our language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We admitted it already as Exhibit D1824.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise then. 000285, can we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to move on to April 1992 and if we have enough time we are going to go back to the autumn of 1991. The 65 ter number is 00285. Talundzic was chief of police in Prijedor until when?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until you expelled him from his job by using weapons, I'm referring to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, sir, I know you're an intelligent man. Give us answers. Until which date?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 30th of April when an armed military coup took place and when power was forcibly taken over in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. I asked you what date. Now, take a look at this, sir, the chief of the regional MUP, Mr. Zupljanin, on the 16th of April says who it is that is supposed to change their insignia and to pledge an oath of allegiance to the new entity and it says the obligations mentioned in this telegram do not apply to the Prijedor and Kotor Varos public security stations. Authorised officials at these stations may continue to wear the current insignia if they wish until further notice, until the political situation in these municipalities is resolved. Do you know that Talundzic had to receive this telegram personally?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume he did get it if regular communications channels were used, however, I did not talk to Talundzic and I do not know if he received it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So insignia were not a problem; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, that is to say, on this date, it says in the telegram, in the dispatch that they can keep their legal and legitimate insignia of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1825, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you the following: Do you know, Mr. Sejmenovic -- actually, did you attend a meeting of the SDA? There were ministers and MPs there and important members of the party. This was on the 10th of June, 1991, at the police building.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to 1991? I attended this meeting in 1991, the one that you're referring to, when the movement for the preservation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and for the protection of Bosnia and Herzegovina was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It could hardly be called that, could it? You established a council for the national prevention [as interpreted] of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not right. This is forgery of the name of that conference. It was for the preservation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not for the Muslims of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The persons who were present there were of Bosniak and Serb and Croat ethnic backgrounds. This was a gathering of academicians of the Academy of Sciences and Arts of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of all prominent persons who wished to attend that gathering, ministers, MPs and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Give me the name of one single Serb.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know just off-the-cuff who the members were. I just know that they were present and that part of them took part in the debate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Give me just one single name.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you now, I cannot even enumerate all the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just give me yes or no answers. It's no problem if you don't know. Just tell me if you know. So do you know that on the 31st of March a decision was made to establish the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that a decision was made?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who made the decision, but I do know that the Patriotic League as a movement, as a movement, for preserving Bosnia-Herzegovina was indeed established, or rather, an attempt was made to establish it but in effect it never came to life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Movement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Too fast. It's too fast for the interpreters to follow. Mr. Sejmenovic, please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My profound apologies, my profound apologies, and I shall try to facilitate your work as much as I can in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you as well, please wait. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that the Patriotic League, according to the decision reached on the 31st of March, was established on the 30th of April; that on the 10th of June, the political staff of this Patriotic League was established and it was called the Council for National Security. Up until September 1991 Sefer Halilovic established nine regional staffs and about 90 municipal staffs and there was a headquarters. Up until the beginning of the war there was this Patriotic League in 103 municipalities and they all had staffs as well. You just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, and in the municipality of Prijedor, Sefer Halilovic did not establish anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you claim that Sefer Halilovic missed Prijedor altogether and established all of this in the remaining 103 municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, call Sefer Halilovic and ask him. Do not ask me about this particular subject matter that I am not very familiar with. It is not going to be of any use to you or me or the Trial Chamber. I don't wish to improvise. I have said what I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 06708, could I have that, please. That was the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, this is an intelligence report of a certain Milos -- well, no. You will see that he's a professional, impartial. What is described here is all the things that were established, the representatives of Sandzak, Kosovo, Belgrade, foreign countries, the presidents of Municipal Assemblies that were elected by the SDA and also prominent individuals of Muslim ethnicity and then there is a reference to all the persons who were present there because journalists were not allowed access. So obviously a Muslim worked for the secret service. And now what is stated is all the things that were decided. It says that there were different cases of extremists who were not discovered -- actually, were detected in Bosanska Dubica and in Prijedor and that all of that indicates -- indicates that there is co-ordination, agreement -- just a moment, please, let me find this in Serbian. Actually, do you see this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see this, but I don't know who Milos is. I don't know what makes him impartial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You will see.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see how he's a Muslim and the SDA did not have any groups of extremists in Bosnia and Herzegovina and what is stated here unambiguously is that there were groups of extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know these persons, Asim Dizdar [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mirza Mujadzic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Omer Veladzic.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By sight, if that is the man I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Atif Kamber. I can mention a lot of them. Izet Muhamedagic; did you know him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Izet Muhamedagic. He was the justice minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in Serbian and in English?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rusmir Mahmutcehajic, the prime minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina is referred to here as well, and you call these people extremists?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, you know full well that the international community asked for Mahmutcehajic to step out of politics because he was an extremist.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of the requests were addressed to you; however, you did not heed them and that is why all these things happened, all the things on account of which we are all sitting here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you see the other names on this other page here, Asim Dizdar, Omer Veladzic. Can we have the next page in Serbian and leave this page in English?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do see this. Thousands of names could have been written here, but what does this mean? It doesn't mean a thing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that you were at the meeting? You were at the meeting, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there for about half an hour and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha, thank you. So half an hour and then you left. Sir, sir, this is a report of the intelligence service. This Milos appears quite frequently with his impartial names. You will see how he criticises Serbs. He says in the last sentence these activities on arming these persons were made possible by persons from abroad, the Muslims who were temporarily working abroad. Did they receive that or not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These persons, Mahmutcehajic, one of those who were listed here who was the deputy prime minister in the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina received weapons from some persons from abroad. I want to stress once again, sir, to you and to the Trial Chamber, I don't think my mind is restricted and I claim that this playing with the witness one anonymous intelligence document with a number of such formulations should be presented to a witness and that I should be requested to comment on it. There are many things that don't make sense in this document so I would ask the Trial Chamber not to be exposed to this sort of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, it is for you to answer the question as far as you can know, as far as you can answer. And it is for the Chamber to assess the weight of this document later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the penultimate paragraph which says who they are, Jasmin Alicic [phoen] from Tukovo; Adil Ganic [phoen], the owner of this; Slavko Ecimovic; Hasan Talundzic, chief of the Prijedor SJB; the Velici brothers, and so on. Becir Medunjanin from Kozarac. You knew all these people and you met them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the SDA structures in this document from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the deputy prime minister to some municipal members of the SDA. The document contains everyone along the hierarchy from top to bottom. This is what it says and I can conclude that on the first and last names that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see that Sefer Dedic is mentioned here as the commander of the Patriotic League in Rizvanovici and you say that the Patriotic League did not exist there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Sefer Dedic, I have never heard of him. The Patriotic League did not exist in the territory of the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm actually checking. These documents have come up before so I want to check to the extent as possible we have as much consistency in the rulings on this, so if the court will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On the basis of the witness's evidence that he attended the meeting, albeit briefly, cannot be a basis upon which we can admit it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right, that's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1826, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I will read to you a quotation from a book, but the Oslobodjenje newspaper, the Muslim-run Oslobodjenje from Sarajevo is quoted on the 14th of January, 1999. Do you know who Meho Karisik, also known as Kemo, is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the name from the year 1992. I cannot be quite certain, but I suppose, I think, that he was the chief of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here they call him the general commander of the Patriotic League. Please hear what exactly he said. [As read] "We were also convinced into that, this is what Mirza Mujadzic claims to this day and he was the most responsible for this area. Therefore, the Patriotic League could provide stiffer resistance there than it did. It seemed that some people from Sarajevo assessed that in these territories we did not have any chance to resist and that had an impact on the events in the Sana valley to be as they were." So he claims that you did have some forces and that it was possible to do things in a different manner; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, anyone can claim whatever he likes. If these persons watched the situation from a distance or made assessments on the basis of partial information. I was present in the area and I talk very precisely and very openly about things that I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have regular meetings that had to do with Defence preparations in Kozarac and in the local communes around Kozarac, that is to say, rather, in Prijedor and the local communes in Kozarac and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, as part of its authority and part of its responsibilities, did hold regular meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How often and what was the composition of those who attended?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to its own rules and propositions, I was not a member of the Territorial Defence structures, so I cannot say anything in detail about the frequency of these meetings. But I did attend two meetings at which the Territorial Defence together with others, that is to say, the representatives of the local communes, talked about the situation that we found ourselves in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see 65 ter 20186. Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that these are the meetings from the meeting of committee which was composed of these four men and about the distribution of the assistance, that is to say, the funds which were collected abroad; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Something to that sense is in this document. I haven't read all of it, but I see some figures and some names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We could turn to the next page in English, though this page shows that Dr. Mirza Mujadzic received some money from people from foreign countries and now it says that the commission received the money and on behalf of the commission it was Mirza Mujadzic.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He received a certain amount of Deutschemarks. It would be good if we could specify the exact amounts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the exact amount.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was 2.500 Deutschemarks or 1.250 euros in the current value.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the fifth page which is the next one. And one page further, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see what were the funds collected from membership fees from the members who paid membership to the party, which is something usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but we need the following page, please, or rather two page forwards. You can see that Mujadzic and the others signed this. We can see that the money was changed --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to read it over. I have to read it if you will ask me something about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1 million dinars which Alajbegovic gave as a gift to the party?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to say how much 1 million dinars would be today in terms of the worth of the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 300 dinars for 1 Deutschemark, correct, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, 3.000 Deutschemarks. It says that. All right. I've seen it. I've read it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move two pages forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please have a look whether the SDA Prijedor talks about a statement from the forum of citizens and there is an invitation to boycott the work and schools, paying for public utilities and so on and all of that before the take-over of power?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am a founding member of the citizens' forum in Tuzla together with Dr. Enes Sadikovic and with two other Serb citizens so that any invitation of the citizens' forum to boycott anything is something that doesn't make sense at all even though that is what this paper says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the bottom it says, "Set up a new executive committee" and further down: "Support the initiative of the opposition to set up a presidency." Mugbila Besirevic is the co-ordinator; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know who this is. I don't know what they had in mind. This paper is confusing. It is written on the paper with the official heading of the SDA or that was something that was added to this sheet of paper, but the content itself is confusing so I don't know what to say about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In this instance, I can't see the basis in the witness's answers. I have a little trouble with the relevance in any event. So I think that combination of factors seems to militate against admission -- at least that's my assessment based on the review of the answers provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did the witness not confirm that Mujadzic received some certain amount of money?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: He was reading from the document as I understood it. I understood him to say that is what the document said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you will allow me, all parties at that time and even to this day in accordance with legal regulations may receive donations up to a certain amount. It is something quite usual, especially if they cannot finance themselves from regular sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not challenge the content of this document, do you, Mr. Sejmenovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one which is on the screen right now, I find it quite muddled and I don't know what to say about it. I don't see anything logical in it as a basis on which I could comment on it. And the previous paper commented on donations of members of the SDA and I said that that was a usual phenomenon, that all parties always received donations and money and they will continue to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. I was going to add that I had the impression that this was not one document, but a compilation of separate documents and -- which accounts for the fact that the witness has provided different responses to different portions of the 65 ter exhibit, which does not appear to be one integral document. So to the extent the Court is now considering admission, I think they need to be broken down to the separate pages and the individual comments and whether or not any basis exists. I think -- the witness has indicated if I recall correctly in addition to his comment about -- just now about the nature of donations, I think there was a comment as well about membership fees. I don't recall it specifically, but those would seem to be the only two concrete bases for admission of portions of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, while you are standing, do you see the bottom left part in English page voluntary contributions Essen.doc/JTR. Or Mr. Karadzic, can you explain what this is about?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Gladly. These are the minutes concerning the work of the organs of the Party of Democratic Action Prijedor. The first document is dated the 30th of March and at the bottom of the page it says that a computer shall be bought and that the money would be deposited on the account of the Crisis Staff. The Crisis Staff was to say which account that would be. So that was a donation for the needs of the Crisis Staff on the 30th of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not see that document. I would like to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let's go back to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second page is better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the first page. What does "Essen" mean? Can you answer that, what "Essen" in the first page is? Why don't you zoom in further, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it says here "voluntary contributions for the SDA party."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And "Essen," what does it -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was going to -- I didn't want to pre-empt the witness, but for what it's worth I note that we have a stamp of the SDA Westfalen and clearly an indication of an area in Germany and Essen would also be a town in Germany. I can't -- I'm not indicating I know specifically that those two are related, but it's a difficult contextual relationship to ignore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then next page. It refers first to something in relation to Prijedor, 30th ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English, we might have a look at the second page, but this all has to do with Prijedor and in Serbian I can see it. But perhaps the second page in English where it says that the computer which has not yet been bought, that the money should be deposited on the account of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll take a break and during the break I would like Mr. Robinson to have a discussion with Mr. Tieger as to the way how this is to be dealt with, given that this is a compilation -- seems to be a compilation of various kinds of documents. We'll resume at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Dr. Karadzic would like to explain to you the relevance of that document in context or in connection with other documents that he wishes to put to this witness, but he wants to do that outside of the presence of the witness which is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before he does that, could you explain to us as to the -- how that document was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that document was admitted as a Defence exhibit in the Stakic case and it appears -- it may also have been admitted in the Tadic appeals because if you see it bears the number at the top "IT-94-1-A" and it was all compiled in one exhibit in the Stakic case at least and then in one 65 ter number by the Prosecution which is where we got it from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, but the question was not the relevance itself but the foundation on which we can admit this document based upon this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's a separate issue from authenticity and that's one that also -- perhaps Mr. Tieger would like to be heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I feel like my rising -- I was -- it was a bit anticipatory, so I don't want to cut off Mr. Robinson's comments. I just have two quick comments. I don't think anybody is aware of how this document was compiled. It was apparently originally submitted by the Defence in Tadic so no one in the Stakic case was in any position to identify how exactly each document in that compilation may be related to one another or precisely where they came from. And secondly the discussion in the Stakic case clearly reveals that its admission in that case - and I brought to Mr. Robinson's attention the fact that it was admitted - had nothing to do with the underlying authenticity. It was clear that none of the participants were in a position to talk about that. And after some discussion about the document it was sort of admitted out of inertia simply because the document had been discussed. So although I appreciate that there are circumstances where the admission -- many circumstances, in fact, where the admission of a document in a previous case has a great deal to do with a document's underlying authenticity, this does not appear to be one of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can bring in the witness. In the meantime --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is not helpful at the moment, Mr. Karadzic. Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not about the document, about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was about to give the ruling as to this document. Yeah, we'll admit this. Just a second. Given that this document was admitted in previous trials and hearings -- proceedings in one package and that we have certain degree of a foundation from this witness upon which we can admit this document, this will be -- and separate from the issue of weight which will be given to this document, the Chamber is of the view we have basis to admit this. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1827, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, when did you set up Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: When did you set up war staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] War staffs were never established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when were war Crisis Staffs formed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. All that was set up was set up inside and within the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at 65 ter 20185.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the take-over by the Serbs in Prijedor, did you carry out preparations for war?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the take-over by the Serbs in Prijedor, the only action was strictly according to the instructions of the republic leadership and the republic institutions whenever possible. As far as defence was concerned then it was action through the structures of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come back to that, but please answer my questions only. Did you carry out preparations for war before the take-over?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence, in keeping with the orders of the republic staff for Territorial Defence, carried out activities and its organisational affairs, preparing for defence within its purview and its competencies as prescribed by the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the 4th of April Mr. Izetbegovic proclaimed general mobilisation? We don't need to debate this. Just tell me, do you know that on the 4th of April before the recognition of Bosnia's independence, Mr. Izetbegovic proclaimed general mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic did not proclaim anything. The Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina proclaimed an immediate threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not general mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any mobilisation. I know about the decision of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina to proclaim an immediate threat of war. I don't know if it was exactly on the 4th of April, but I repeat it was the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will now put to you the chronology of events. On the 4th of April, Mr. Izetbegovic, or rather, a part of the Presidency, contrary to the veto imposed by Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Koljevic proclaimed general mobilisation. On the 6th of April he replaced General Vukosavljevic as commander of the Territorial Defence. On the 8th of April he set up a new Territorial Defence and proclaimed an immediate threat of war. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct. The first thing you said on the 4th of March --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true because the full Presidency was still operating. Furthermore, on the 6th of April no new Territorial Defence was set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I didn't say it was.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said a new Territorial Defence was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat. On the 6th, General Vukosavljevic, a Serb, was replaced. On the 8th a new Territorial Defence was set up and immediate threat of war was proclaimed. On the 12th the new commander sent a new directive for an attack against the Serbs and the JNA. Is that correct?
