utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct. Your Honours, I'm facing heavy manipulation here and it is my obligation in my present position to react to this manipulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm interested in your knowledge, not your opinion. Do you know or don't you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Sejmenovic, if you do not agree with the question put to you by Mr. Karadzic, you can say so. Yes, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please allow me, Your Honour, to say that I don't agree with the form of the questions put to me. Let's take a specific example. The last question said that a directive by the Territorial Defence ordered an attack against the Serbs and the JNA. That is an extremely heavy instance of manipulation that reminds me of times past. Nobody ordered an attack against the Serbs. The order was to defend ourselves from the JNA, from attacks by the JNA. That commander of the Territorial Defence was replaced. Another manipulation is to put to me that a new Territorial Defence was formed. It was still the same Territorial Defence, only the commander who had been under the control of Belgrade was replaced and some officers who were still in JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have a whole document that I have no time to show to you that proves this.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have time for everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just tell me it didn't happen. That's an answer too. Do you know that the Serb side set up a Territorial Defence only on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of April the Serb side did not have to set up a Territorial Defence because the Territorial Defence existed equally in all areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, that's a political argument.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a political argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you do you know about it.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that internal decision of yours. It was not my position to know it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 65 ter 20185. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see it is a report about the work of the regional Crisis Staff from its last meeting to date. Distribution of procured assets. The work of daily patrols, military police, report about Kozarusa, Kozarac, Trnopolje, Kevljani, Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are misreading this. I can see this. Item 1 is a report on the local Crisis Staff which before the war and after was a unit of the Territorial Defence, a local Crisis Staff, and the date is 26 April and ten days before that the republic leadership ordered the mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and its reinforcement so that it be able to efficiently defend the area where people live.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that work is being done to set up a military police force? Do you see that private businessman Bahonjic says that private businessmen should pay to the account of the local commune on account of taxes funds to support the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about some sort of police but not the police that you suggest. This meeting was attended also by the police commander in Kozarac. According to orders from the republic leadership from the legal institution of Territorial Defence, it was ordered that all defence capacities be integrated in the area. That was the police and the war-time police which also existed under the law dating back to pre-war times and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look, Kozarac, the purpose of this meeting -- I have to read it in English.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Read it in our language for my sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Co-ordination. Everybody should do their part of the job. Causevic says: "I have been left alone without the Assembly."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Without the president of the local Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He does not -- it's very difficult to make out but it is available in English.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it before me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page in Serbian. There it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doesn't it say something about the purchase of arms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I see this page displayed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is displayed. Purchasing seven Zolja hand-held launchers.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do not put in terms that are not there. It doesn't say "purchase" anywhere. There's just a list of various weapons. Where did you find the word "purchase"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll find it. "The Executive Board should buy ..."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regulator for pumps, which is fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then they list what needs to be bought.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not bought. That's what you say. It just says Zolja, RPG, automatic rifles. Please do not misread this document in our language. I read very well and I even know the context of these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So these Zolja launchers fell from the sky? They were not bought?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the weapons that the Territorial Defence had. At that time there was an immediate threat of war, we were surrounded at that time by you with all kinds of weapons and the Territorial Defence was to protect its population as it was its obligation. And I repeat, protect and defend.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page. I think we need the next page in English too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Doesn't it say here "procured two Zolja, 300 Deutschemark?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it reads that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Two automatic rifles; RPGs, 30 Deutschemark. Was this purchased?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was purchased, I believe, from your soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Territorial Defence purchased this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted as Exhibit D1828.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you continue to claim you did not have war time Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the local staff of the Territorial Defence which received orders on the 14th or perhaps earlier to organise themselves to move into immediate threat of war mode and to use all capacities in case they are attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did this happen even before the immediate threat of war was proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That started happening from the moment when the republic Territorial Defence issued orders to take such action. Before that in the institutions of local communes or political parties, there was no such action.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did the republic TO issue that order?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, sometime in early April.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992 or perhaps even a bit earlier. I'm not sure now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 20191, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Sejmenovic, did you use the public auditing agency to abuse joint funds?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The public auditing agency functioned normally until you manipulated it to redirect the funds to Gradiska and Banja Luka, your towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look, in October 1991, 24 October 1991, you see assignments to weapons duty, Kozarac, Kenjar and Bahonjic; Trnopolje, Sead Sivac; Kozarusa, Tadzic; Brdo and Ljubija, Kadiric, Hopovac, Sikiric; Puharska, Rufad Suljanovic. And then it says Dr. Eso something --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say something about the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have to introduce this man. On the 24th of October and 30th October on behalf of the Prijedor local commune a proposal is made to hold the congress in Sarajevo on the 6th of September to recruit -- I'll read in English because I can't see the original. "[In English] Recruits to stay within BH. "Records to be removed. "Organise a 'women's committee' (Kevic Sikiric Sivac)". [Interpretation] So this should be organised and there is something about the Yugoslav People's Army as well. So recruits should stay in Bosnia and military records should be removed and some women's committee is supposed to be organised. And these ladies, Kevic, Sikiric, and Sivac are supposed to take part in that. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not right. This document was written subsequently or forged all together. There are five dates here and out of these dates one says that it is the year that comes afterwards. It's as if I were to be writing 2012 now. The first date read 1992 and then it was corrected to read 1991. See here. And then further down, again, you have 1992 and then it was corrected to state 1991. This is one of the elements why I doubt this particular document. Secondly, Rufad Suljanovic had nothing to do with this. The third element: The person referred to here is Sead Sivac had absolutely nothing to do with any of this. We saw each other every day. So as far as this particular piece of paper is concerned, there is really no point in my commenting on it. If you think that you should use it, use it any which way you want, but it was my duty to explain these facts to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about Eso and Tadzic, were they appointed to this committee for dealing with refugees in Prijedor 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SDA did have this initiative, made a proposal to the SDS in 1991, that we try to work together to take care of the refugees that were coming to our region from Croatia. That is a fact, but I'm talking about this particular record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that item 4 says to be against mobilisation and there's also a threat issued with the UN in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really see any point in any of this. The Hague Tribunal was founded considerably later and somebody here refers to a threat with The Hague. This seems a bit ridiculous -- no, not a bit ridiculous, totally ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, there was this conference that was held in The Hague before that and this is a threat with this conference in The Hague, not the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you needed some municipal committee to issue threats to you? Please, I would not want us to have a discussion at this level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see here that there is a reference to the fund for physical education, 100 billion dinars were supposed to be transferred for the functioning of the plebiscite and Tadzic was in charge of that; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written there. Now who wrote this up, and for what reason, that is not something I can say on the basis of this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was Tadzic, what office did he hold?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which Tadzic? There were several of them. There was a Tadzic in the SDA, some lower-ranking official. If that's the Tadzic that you mean, he was a low-ranking official in the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that Dr. Mujadzic says that a car should be bought for Mujadzic and that some Deutschemarks should be exchanged and so on and so forth. But on the 23rd of September, 1991, a war Crisis Staff for Prijedor had Refik Krkic and Cazim Pezo appointed to it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, not then or later did the SDA establish any Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that was either forged or somebody was forced to write this up. This has nothing to do with reality and you can treat it any which way you want. Had there been a staff, I would have explained, I would have said who the members are, just as I did in the case of bodies that actually existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that on the 23rd of September a state of emergency was proclaimed in war-time conditions, Cazim Pezo, and down here 12th of May, Hambarine, if the local commune cannot meet Sefik Krkic and Cazim Pezo will make decisions and Mirza signed that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is stated on this piece of paper is totally incorrect. There was no state of war proclaimed on the 23rd of February 1991 or imminent threat of war. Imminent threat of war was declared later. And I claim with total conviction to this Trial Chamber that it was only later that something was charged with writing up a chronology based on semi-knowledge in respect of the events involved. This is so telling. An imminent threat of war was declared only later. At this point in time there was no mention of any such thing, any kind of state of emergency or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. We are going to ask the OTP to explain this to us because they placed this on the 65 ter list but we don't have to tire you with all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it is for you to explain to the Chamber as to the nature of that document first, at all. What is your case, Mr. Karadzic? Do you argue this is a minute of meetings, as entitled in the e-court?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, it is absolutely clear that this is an excerpt from SDA minutes that have to do with defence preparations. Several dates are referred to there so they recorded when they did what in terms of preparing for war. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then it is for you to lay foundation in relation to that. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This was rejected by the Stakic Chamber. Judge Sch omburg said we consider this or believe it to be a forgery and we don't want to see it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then we are going to ask for expertise with regard to this manuscript. We are going to ask for papers of SDA officials to be sent or handed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is for you how to put -- lay foundation in relation to this document, but at the moment we don't have any basis to admit this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like the Prosecution to explain the chain of custody to us, how this document was obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it this was offered by the Defence and it was rejected by the previous Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's my understanding, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to skip certain things, Mr. Sejmenovic. Now I have to deal with some of the things that you said. You said in the Tadic case 1310 is the page reference, the 23rd of May, 1996, you said that the Serb Radical Party did not become part of this list but then you also said in the Stakic case when you testified that the SDS and the Serb Radical Party left parliament. Are you trying to say that the Serb Radical Party was in parliament and in the authorities in 1990?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which parliament are you talking about? The year is wrong at any rate. It could have been a mistake in the transcript. Perhaps I made a slip of the tongue if I said "1990." I beg your pardon. I would like to know what level you're talking about, the municipality or the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: November 1991. The SDS and the Serb Radical Party left parliament?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that is a mistranslation, a mistranslation. I said that they walked out, or rather, they had this particular candidate for the chamber of municipalities. The SDS did not have a candidate of their own. They reached agreement with the Radical Party that their candidate should be the joint candidate of those two parties for the chamber of municipalities. There is an audio recording of that and you can hear that very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So that was in 1990, he was part of our list?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. Because only one person went from the municipality and that was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it was the elections of 1990.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to focus a bit. In the first multi-party elections, that's the election that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Serb Radical Party did not exist up until, say, 1991 and they ran in the elections in Serbia only in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prijedor, that is not correct. The gentleman who was one of the founders of the Serb Radical Party in Prijedor from the Tomasica or Omarska neighbourhoods was -- I simply cannot remember his name now, but you do have his name in the transcript. I knew him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't have time and we have proof of the fact that it had not existed at least a year after the elections. You talked about brigades and the garrison in Prijedor and also about these brigades returning from the front line, especially the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked about one brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell the Trial Chamber, is it correct that the garrison in Prijedor was the basic garrison for the 5th Kozara and the 43rd Motorised Brigades?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the military position was of that garrison in terms of the military profession, that is something I did not know. But what I said was that this garrison existed in Prijedor before the war as well and JNA soldiers stayed in that garrison even before the war, but there were very few -- very, very few of them, perhaps a dozen or so soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that is the peacetime 5th Kozara Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did we -- or rather, did you hide around the villages in Prijedor; and if so, how long?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the villages above Trnopolje. I hid there for about a month, up to a month and a half maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you the only official of the SDA, the only Muslim adversary of the Serb government that was hiding or were there more of you?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area where I was, I was all alone in contact with part of the remaining population, or rather, refugees. And towards the end of that period I was totally alone. What happened on the other side in the town of Prijedor and in the suburbs and the west, that I did not know. I did hear some information over a transistor radio, some members of the SDA managed to get to the territory of Bihac others remained in Sarajevo. Those who were captured during the first days, that is to say in the initial period, I heard of their fate only later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the 29th of April a telegram arrived from the minister of defence and from the minister of the interior to start the attack in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that particular document here. It was shown to me. I was not well-versed because I did not hold any executive office in Prijedor. I did not know about this particular subject matter so I was not very useful to the court from that point of view. I can only speculate. I cannot present any truth with regard to that document because I was not familiar with any such facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who would be opposed to it, or rather, who would be the enemy if this were to be carried out? Who would you be firing at, the Territorial Defence of Kozarac, et cetera, if this were to have succeeded?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In respect of this theoretical question, I can only say the following. The Territorial Defence in Kozarac did not have Serbs as their enemy on the other side, especially not the Serb people. They only had fear and they tried to save the people in the area that was under its control, save them from massacres that were already taking place in neighbouring municipalities. That's the only thing that the Territorial Defence had. They had these provocations against them. They did not have an actual enemy so they did not set out to fight against an enemy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have 1D2942.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we are given enough time, Mr. Sejmenovic, we are going to show very nicely through your own documents what the objective was. Please take a look at this document dated the 15th of April and look at this. The garrison command in Prijedor. And then it says inter-ethnic relations are becoming ever more complicated, that's the second paragraph. And the third paragraph is that: [As read] "The most flagrant example are organised armaments of individuals and groups of all ethnic backgrounds and the establishment of paramilitary and para-political forces with pronounced nationalist characteristics." And then it says further down: [As read] "Keep members of the JNA from inter-party interest because in that way we're going to preserve our units and contribute to improved security in the region. Do not allow anyone to manipulate our units and to use them in any struggle for personal, party, or other particular interests. "4. Raise combat-readiness to the highest level and stand ready to defend military facilities, the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks in Prijedor, the military warehouses in Pancic [phoen], Svodna, the repeater, the communication nodes in Kozara, as well as the garrison infirmary." Can we have the next page now, please. Under item 5 he requests that a part of the unit, the 343rd motorised one should return to its home garrison. And under item 6 it says without special order of the commander of the 2nd Military District no one can distribute weapons to the Territorial Defence but consider the announcement of seizing weapons from military depots and take measures to prevent such activities. And then further on about the intentions and activities of the JNA and then under 9 it says organise for me a meeting with the authorities, the leadership of the SUP and the municipal staff of Territorial Defence and insist that the meeting be attended by the representatives of all parties from the area and the topic of the meeting shall be the place and role of JNA units in the prevention and expansion of inter-ethnic conflicts and so on and so forth. Major Radmilo Zeljaja, the 15th of April. He issued the order on that date. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that document now. I didn't know that it existed there. I wasn't aware of it. I know that the document says one thing and the very same Radmilo Zeljaja and his military units were doing something quite different in the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at the time the Muslims and the Croats did not respond to call-ups to join the JNA and that the army which Zeljaja had at his disposal was composed mostly of Serbs and a few Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radmilo Zeljaja wrote this document on the day when the UN Security Council declared that an aggression had been committed in Bosnia-Herzegovina by the JNA. On the very same day Zeljaja sat down and wrote this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you this. I'm asking you whether the Croat and Muslim lads were at their homes whereas the Serbian young men were in his units.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all at their homes -- may I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I may be too kind if I were to give this warning to you, but you have spent two hours and not touched upon a single matter discussed in his examination-in-chief, in particular those in relation to the scheduled incident or his detention. You cannot complain about shortage of time, bear that in mind. I'm still struggling to understand how relevant this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, the witness was not arrested or taken prisoners just so. He surrendered himself, but what is at stake here is what he and his party had created as an atmosphere and as a development and how come it is not important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued]...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then why did Mr. Tieger ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I will leave it in your hands. You understand that the Chamber has been lenient as to the Defence strategy. The witness testified that the various killings or various ill-treatment, et cetera. So one may ask you whether this is the reason for such treatment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, what is the mass grave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We'll mark for identification this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1829, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will first finish with what you're interested in and then I will ask for time to cover what Mr. Tieger asked the witness about, the events and preparations. What is the mass grave in which the four brothers were found?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which one they were found, but I read the list of the buried persons and they were buried in one of the collective burials. You can find the records very easily. I think it's available on the internet. So I think you can sit down and find the information or you can call one of the associations of the people who are looking for their missing relatives or the institute for victims in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they will provide you with that immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You are testifying so I have to ask you because you introduced this topic. You said that they were found in a mass grave. In which mass grave were they found?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you, I have no need or reason to analyse the details and information about all the victims as to the mass grave in which they were found. The fact that they were exhumed and buried indicates that the teams who work on that found them in one of the graves and transported them, identified them, and that they have been buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you seen the occasion on which they died?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I heard shots and I saw the man who buried them on a following morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if you heard shots and if an inmate of Trnopolje or the prisoner, however we call him, means they were buried close to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were liquidated close to a location we call Beslaga's mill, close to a little bridge. That was where the execution took place and somewhere close by they were interred. Now, where the bodies were transferred later on and whether that happened once or twice or three times in order to cover up, I wouldn't know. But I know that after 10 or 15 years they have been found or that is to say the majority in the Bosnian Krajina, those who are looked after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you, you didn't see the murder. Which murder did you see with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see the murders personally. I did not see any shooting personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me tell you now, Mr. Sejmenovic, all you testify in this manner, they took somebody out and later on shots were heard or they took someone away and he never returned. Can you please tell me what you did see?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained on a number of occasions what I did see. I was present when their names were called out, when they left, and I saw that they did not return. We heard shots. In the morning we learned that they had been liquidated. I'm talking about one particular case, and today if you sit into a car and pass by the graveyard in Kamicani, if anyone is doubtful about some of these people, you can read their names there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And something else, there is a witness here and can you please address me as a witness and not to tell me all you witnesses. I'm not all the witnesses. I'm just a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did we see each other in Banja Luka when Mr. Kupresanin took you there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We were close to one another but we didn't see one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you describe some of my disagreements with the SDS in Prijedor concerning that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described a disagreement which was expressed by your deputy, Srdjo Srdic with regard to you and a disagreement expressed by Vojo Kupresanin, again with regard to you, and I interpreted that as fully as I could recollect and it is very clearly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You confirmed that Kupresanin called someone or someone called him from Omarska and that they talked about bars of soap and so on. Were there any other presidents before the president of the republic that he could have asked that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't have asked the president of the municipality because the municipal officials came to Omarska, they were present there, the chief of the police and so on. The police which guarded the camp had their superior in Banja Luka at each and every moment. Kupresanin was an official from Banja Luka and he certainly didn't address himself on that telephone. He was talking with a president. In my testimony I then said that he was called because the president was looking for him. I'm not sure whether it was said President Karadzic. I'm talking about the telephone conversation which he had inside the Omarska camp. I heard clearly that he said that beds and bars of soap were necessary and so on, but later on he told me that he would contact you. He contacted you while I was sitting maybe 3 or 4 metres from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But from the administration building in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he tell you that I had asked him to see to it that those who were behind the rebellion should be placed in home imprisonment and should have decent conditions and that after that you were under house arrest in a village?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that you told him anything about conditions of any kind. I don't remember that. You told him to provide clothes for me. He told you that he had already decided to get the clothes, that he should make it possible for me to recuperate, to fatten up, that was the exchange you had and a few things you had like all right, all right, fine, okay. That was what I heard, that was the context of your conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the conclusion that it was me who could have been talking with Kupresanin at the time, what month was that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was early August 1990 -- 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you claim that telephone lines between Banja Luka and Sarajevo existed in early August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only between Banja Luka and Sarajevo but between Banja Luka and Zenica, Banja Luka and Tuzla, all these telephone lines operated. He confirmed that to me and he offered, or rather, requested me to call some numbers in Sarajevo if I wanted to reach someone, if I had anyone there, and he suggested that through me he should contact people in Zenica and Tuzla because of electricity and some other needs. He also offered me to call some of my acquaintances in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown a video-clip from Trnopolje. You entered Trnopolje on two occasions; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you whether you remember when Bozanic asked you whether Penny Marshall and British journalists were a bit further away from Mutic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. In the video-clip I couldn't recognise Penny Marshall and whether they were British journalists that was something I learned later. I learned later which news agency that was and all the specific details. But at the moment when they entered, we knew they were foreign journalists. We all called them foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember the cart and the building tools?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the building tools actually fenced off or wired off with a wire?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the video-clip -- perhaps I would need to see it again to see whether that was outside or inside the wiring, but as for the wheelbarrow or the cart I can say the following. Before the war it was a shop selling agricultural equipment and there were many wheelbarrows there. Some of the wheelbarrows were later on, with the approval of the camp authorities, used by the non-Serbs. They were allowed to take a wheelbarrow, go to their own gardens and then dig out potatoes and so on so that those who were the inmates would feed off that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm saying that the wiring through which Penny Marshall interviewed the inmates of Trnopolje was used to wire off the depot of agricultural tools and equipment rather than Trnopolje itself?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment, or rather, while I was in Trnopolje, people, inmates, camp inmates were inside the depot. When the first group was released from Keraterm it was transferred to Trnopolje, placed inside the wiring, and all of them were strictly prohibited from leaving the wired area. And it was called the quarantine by the camp authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How large is the area that was wired off where the wheelbarrows were? How big is it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say off the top of my head, but we can see that in the video-clip so that I wouldn't be guessing. We have a way to establish exactly how big it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was the only area that was wired off; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. A major part on another side was also wired off from the camp in the direction of Trnopolje, that is, and a section in the direction of the railroad tracks did not have wiring at that time or later. It was just an empty area that was right along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I tell you that several adjacent buildings had their own fences and that Trnopolje, itself, did not have its fence, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the places where Trnopolje did not have its own wire fence, there were machine-gun barrels that were directed at the inmates. There were groups of guards which were changed every two or three hours in these places and the locations of the positions of armed men and machine-gun nests is something I cannot list. These were the ones I was aware of. Later on I learned there were others that I wasn't aware of at the time I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that by a miracle your mother survived even though the Serbs were told that she was your mother, and then you also said that you were afraid for 15 of your friends in Trnopolje, you were afraid that they could be liquidated because they protected you; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were told that precisely. They did not look after me, but they contacted me when I entered the camp and they were requested to say where I was at the moment and they didn't know that because I had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And so you claim that your mother could have been liquidated and your friends as well just because the you were the goal of the Serbian forces and you were captured but were not liquidated, that is to say you reported and were not liquidated. How do you account for that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very easy. Most liquidations and murders took place in the first 20 days when the military forces ethnically destroyed the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you that. How come that you say that those who assisted you would be liquidated and you who are the main hero there have not been liquidated?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, because I could observe the behaviour and conduct of your forces for days and days and days on end and I didn't have a single reason to think anything else. The circumstances, or rather, God's will decided that I would fall into the hands of these authorities at a quite late stage. They told me that themselves. And as for my mother and the circumstances under which she was taken prisoner, it has nothing to do with what we are discussing now. And there were four clips of ammunition that were shot at her but not a single bullet hit her. She managed to run away and that's how she survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I recounted only one bit of the story, that she survived.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'm under time pressure and this will be another witness that will not have been examined fully. Would you please grant me another session or at least an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's exactly the part which is not acceptable. You have spent, if not wasted, two -- more than two hours and then you cannot complain your time is short. You will have exactly three hours, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You've said that you were close to a military column overhearing them talk and you make a long statement about what they were saying, and all that while they were passing by. How come?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I overheard that conversation because I was hiding. In fact, I had started to run and then I didn't have enough time. I quickly found cover, a small earthen house with a garage beside it. That group that was on foot came close to the garage, shot at the lock, trying to open the door to see if there was a car inside they could drive away. After several attempts they got it open, saw there were no car, and went on. While they were only approaching the garage and while they were trying to open the door, I heard that part of their conversation. I don't know if it's useful or not, but I told all I'd heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said first they were passing by and now you say they stopped by the garage.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened twice. Once there was a large group with an APC walking that was on the road to Sivci village by the road close to the Krajina church. There I just lay on the ground quickly plucked some grass, covering myself with it, and then I watched them going along the road and looking to see what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can Mr. Mutic confirm about -- confirm what you said about him, about Kozarski Vjesnik and the events in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's up to Mr. Mutic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic's microphone appears to be deactivated or he didn't turn it on so that seems to be the problem why no translation is coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. If it is convenient then we will take a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just ask this question if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 56 the witness said the Serb troops killed a certain number of people. All these are vague answers and I should like -- because all this has to be verified.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Fine. We'll do it after the break then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 25 minutes and resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly for technical reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We go back to open session. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I could just note that we don't oppose the Prosecution's motion for leave to reply to the 92 quater motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wanted to deal with it at the end but that's granted. Did you follow, Mr. Tieger? Your motion to leave to reply was granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, you have 40 minutes to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, during that conversation of Kupresanin allegedly with me, was the speaker-phone on or did you hear my voice, as you say, from the receiver?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the receiver.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you said at some point, let me not look for a reference now, that it sounded like my voice?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I didn't hear it clearly enough to make out everything that was being said by the voice from the receiver, but I heard the timbre of the voice and I'm sure it was your voice but most importantly Kupresanin said it was you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly see 1D357, English page 5, Serbian page 7. D1357. Serbian 7, English 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Second paragraph from the bottom where it says that in the beginning of the war the work of the party was put on stand-by on orders from Pale and then the next paragraph says: [As read] "At the time of combat operation and the freeze of party activity, there was no contact with the head office of the party or with the state leadership of the Serbian Republic so that municipal officials who enjoyed the trust of the SDS were for the most part left to their own devices in decision-making and finding solutions without any guide-lines or a general guide-line from the level of the Serbian Republic. The communications were restored only in September 1992." Do you believe me now that there were no contacts?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly, I doubt the veracity of this document. Between Sarajevo and Banja Luka there was certainly contact and between Prijedor and Banja Luka certainly there was contact. In fact, what I'm trying to say is contact was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between Prijedor and Banja Luka, it's 40 kilometres. It's the same centre. But with Sarajevo, it's much longer. Did you have contact with Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You had telephone communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the SDS and the JNA used to say the same things. Is it true, however, that you said that at meetings between 30th April and 30th May that you had with the SDS and the JNA, the SDS was unable to begin a meeting before a JNA representative arrived and the JNA took the chair at all the meetings?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the president of the SDS did not wish to start the meeting, not that he was unable to. We wanted to start the meeting and he would say some other people are supposed to arrive and those other people were garrison commander, commander of the 5th Kozara Brigade, security men, intelligence men, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And they took the chair?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see 65 ter 1038. That's it. Look at this, please, 23rd April. The Municipal Board of SDS Prijedor, there are various items, but please look at item 6. [As read] "Make it clear that if Zeljaja (JNA) does not state that the JNA shall protect the Serbian people, then the SDS would call upon all Serb soldiers to leave the JNA and take their weapons with them. The SDS asks the Regional Board of the SDS to activate itself as the political authorities in Krajina." Do you see that there is no certainty how the SDS will act at this point?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not only certainty; they had well-laid plans by that time and what is written in these minutes they wrote for needs best known to them. The facts do not support this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I understand your position, but these are minutes from the meeting. It's not a newspaper article.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, of course, say that that's what's written here, but you asked me for a comment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit D1830.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I add something? If we can scroll back to the beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 23rd April, 1992 it says. That's the date when the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army, officially withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina, several days after. It withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina, if I remember well, on the 18th of April and the forces present there were no longer the Yugoslav People's Army. That is an internationally known fact. This was some sort of paramilitary beyond and outside of the laws of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was not the JNA. At the same time it's eight days after the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina was officially proclaimed to be an aggression by decision of the UN Security Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who then took over, assumed power, on the 30th of April and who ordered an attack against the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All important functions, civilian and military, in the Prijedor municipality that morning after the armed take-over were in the hands of people who were either members or associates of the SDS. When I say that I assert with full responsibility I was there and I heard statements, both commander of the 5th Kozara Brigade and garrison commander Radmilo Zeljaja had the same purpose, the same objective, as the SDS. It was one single group, the same machinery that was quite capable of taking over the whole town within 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to argue with you. I'm going only to say that the JNA withdrew on the 19th of May and you say 18th of April, right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 18th of May, yes, but you just asked me about April now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are minutes of 23rd April, where the SDS asks that the JNA make its position clear. You say it was not the JNA, that it was Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, that’s right. However, several days after that we met with these commanders. We know what they told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between the 30th of April and in the course of May and in June did you continue to meet with people from the Territorial Defence of Kozarac, Kozarusa and the other surrounding Muslim local communes?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June those people were detained in camps or had been killed already so there were no meetings in July. There were meetings in May until the all-out artillery attack against Kozarac and Hambarine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with those people between the 30th April and 30th May and later in June?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June, I don't know that anybody was able to meet with anybody. In May, a couple of days before the attack I attended the meeting that we mentioned here several times that was also attended by Commander Zeljaja and Mr. Arsic and your president, Mr. Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 20192, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's another collection of excerpts from SDA minutes. Please look at this. On the 30th of April it says if some groups start provocations in Prijedor, all professional policemen should report to Osman. And then it says Nagib Sivac, Nesib Fazlic and it says they won't hand in their weapons but instead in case of an attack they will defend themselves. Then there is a meeting on the 2nd of May. Can we see the next page. It says the BH Territorial Defence insignia will remain and this man Nagib says many of our men are making provocations. Hasib and another one were shooting yesterday for provocation. The police should arrest them. And this Suljo says that this man is on drugs and then there's a Serb, Dusko Tadic; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it is Dusko Tadic. It could be someone else, but there were Serbs in the TO of Kozarac, two, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see Suljo is talking about the goings on in Kozarusa, about civil disobedience because Serbs were mobilised and they work and then Kenjar says civic disobedience says should also be discussed and then Suljo says below in item 3, that the military police would receive their uniforms on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page. Next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If Kozarusa does not receive assistance, it will surrender all the check-points. Did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give a comment on this record as it is half literate and half articulate. This is about the structure of the Territorial Defence, whose job it was to operate under the rules of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is a reference to check-points here. Did you have check-points and how many around Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it if you didn't try to insinuate that things existed when they did not. Access roads to Prijedor were free of check-points. These check-points referred to here were those that belonged to the TO, and they have the right and duty to hold them. I don't know what their disposition was and what the layout was, but you could find somebody from the TO to explain it. I know about a couple of check-points in my local commune, in my local branch of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there were some in Trnopolje, in Kozarusa, in Hambarine as well because there was an incident there on the 23rd of May?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The TO existed always, throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it had an obligation to hold its own check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, I'm not criticising. Let's see how things were. I'm just telling how things were.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you the facts. I was not part of the command of the Territorial Defence to be able to share with you any details. I've told you what I've seen as an observer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a transcript of the minutes of a meeting of the 4th of March.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not March, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you attend this one?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I've already said I attended several meetings, all of them were very much alike, so it does remind me of one of those meetings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the English version. [In English] Yeah, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at item 3. There's a report that the Serbian MUP proposed a check-point to be set up on the main road, and then below Medunjanin says: "I propose, if Cirkin agrees, that he should take over the regional Crisis Staff -- in fact the local Crisis Staff." Look at what Sivac says. That your command and co-ordination are still poor. Can we see the next page. [In English] Next page in English, please. Did Serbs propose to you that you should establish a Muslim municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've had some proposals. I don't know who exactly made them, but some people insisted that it should be discussed, not to the Muslim municipality but a civic municipality of Prijedor and it's written somewhere in these minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you didn't allow me time to answer your previous two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm happy. You answered what I asked.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the check-point. It was a tank that you sent with live ammunition 10 metres away from the first houses in Kozarac, first with two and then with one soldier in the crew, and there were negotiations to remove the tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I wasn't sending any tanks at that time. It was the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the system. Then you said Sivac speaks about poor command. Of course, because the command was not properly established for those circumstances and that situation, despite the order that had been given to do it. And in the circumstances, it wasn't even possible to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Sivac says something about a rapid reaction company.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says I admit the hierarchy and the command is still poor and he says we will need a rapid reaction company. But let's look at this page, item 3, where it says that the proposal of the Serb chief is to establish a municipality in Kozarac. And [In English] "So that they would not meddle in the work of the bodies." [Interpretation] And Kemo says [In English] [As read] "Only people from Kozarac can create a municipality. Citizens must have their say first of all." [Interpretation] You said to this Trial Chamber that you, Muslims, would have only small farms left. Do you know about the town infrastructure of Prijedor just like the town infrastructure of Sarajevo perhaps would remain shared as in all other towns and according to your own --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just correct something. I did not say private farms would remain. I said that even big farms were represented as Serb-held property. I'm referring to these so-called ekonomija farms as we called them, these large-scale farms. On the map that was made public there was no information to the effect that anything could be shared or joint. It was a propaganda attack. I remember that there was only the green colour and the red colour and maybe a bit of blue, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, the source of your information as a high official should not be a local newspapers; it should be your party structures. Do you know that the old town in the centre of Prijedor was supposed to be within that Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why did your authorities not present that in the newspapers? These newspapers, Kozarski Vjesnik, that was your instrument at the time, very powerful, a lethal one, sowing fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, did you say anything?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Next page, next page in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this. On the 5th of May Beco says: [As read] "All of this is interesting but let's just look at this now. They are offering a municipality that favours them, not us. I agree that on Thursday we should issue a statement about Kozarac as a municipality." So you agree that Kozarac used to be a municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one stage of history, that was a fact, that Kozarac was a municipality. At this point in time, only part of the non-Serbs of Prijedor lived there. A great many others lived in other areas that you're not even mentioning, Ljubija, Hambarine, Rizvanovici, Carakovo, Hambarine, not to mention all of them. But the Serb authorities are only speaking about Kozarac here for reasons of their own. The intentions were clear to us and quite evident. Because we did not get any specific argument that was buttressed by good intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that after the take-over of authorities in Prijedor itself, the Croat-Muslim structure took over the police station in Ljubija and reinforced it?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about what happened in that part of Prijedor. I know that there was some speculation in that regard. What exactly happened I don't know. I don't know what the truth actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Serb side in Kozarski Vjesnik sent a message to the minority Serbs in that area, that they should accept that and that they should be peaceful and loyal?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat once again, I don't know anything about what was going on in Ljubija and I don't know anything about that article. I've never read it. Maybe it was shown to me here, but I cannot give a proper opinion of that because I don't know what happened at the local police station in Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just need your answer. When the time comes, I'm going to show this to the Trial Chamber. And what about the 6th of June, were you at the meeting of the local commune of Kozarac and Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of June Kozarusa was torched, or rather, most of it was razed to the ground. There were no people left there. Kozarac was destroyed and I don't think there was any meeting that was held on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the 6th of June here, the meeting held. All of this can be of interest. The Crisis Staff of Kozarac consists of all citizens from all parties --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is May, not June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The sixth day of the sixth month.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there, but this subject matter has to do with what was going on in May. There were physically no people there and the area was razed to the ground. There was no way a meeting could have been held there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this, Sejmenovic, and you say that you see two solutions: Insignia or no insignia. Who is going to protect you if you surrender your weapons? Many people would get killed. If we choose to procrastinate, [In English] "We have to make all possible effort. I am against the idea that people are left unprotected. I would rather we tried to defend ourselves." [Interpretation] That's what you said; right?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course and that's what I think to this day. I want to have the people protected, any people from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 22nd of May Aziz Aliskovic and 11 other territorials - let us call them that if you refer that - fired at reservists, four Croats and two Serbs, who were passing there in a car and they killed two and seriously wounded two others and lightly wounded two others?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact remains that there was this incident at Hambarine. It is a fact that the Serb authorities interpreted this in one way and the non-Serb population living there had a completely different interpretation. Now, it is not for me to say on the basis of what the truth can be established. I just know that there was this big power on one side. Also I know that your paramilitaries passed through these areas, that they were firing all the time, and this looks like a scenario of starting a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, they killed themselves, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but they used shells to destroy an entire hill that was populated by hundreds of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a call for the surrender of the killers? Wasn't that the ultimatum or requirement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details. I repeat once again, I was in Trnopolje at the time. It was only on the following day that I could see large parts of the hill, Rakovcani, Rizvanovici, Hambarine, Bircan, on fire and I saw the artillery firing at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see Suljo making conciliatory proposals, saying if it's the problem of the flag it's not really a problem, it's important to have guarantees of peace. And then Suljo says down here if they do not hand over their weapons, they will be considered to be a paramilitary. So it is clear to Suljo that if they do not hand over their weapons they will be considered paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: See, now you know what Suljo understands on the basis of this and I don't. And I attended the meetings and I knew what the atmosphere was. So, Your Honours, we are either going to observe the chronology involved or we are going to point out that we are not doing that. Beforehand we spoke about the period of the attack and then, yet again, I have this document placed in front of me that is a document from before that attack when attempts were being made in Banja Luka and Prijedor to safe-guard the population. In the future I kindly ask that we observe the chronology involved or perhaps it should be pointed out that we are moving backwards rather than proceed in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we see that it says the 6th of May, not the 6th of June, so it's a different meeting?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a same meeting, the same handwriting, the same person taking the minutes, it's probably the same document, I don't know, consisting of several pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next one, see, 6th of May. And [In English] This should be accepted and added to the statement. I am particularly glad to see that the Serbs agree with the inclusion of these villages in the civil municipality of Kozarac." [Interpretation] So Serbs agreed that all Muslim-populated locations should be linked to the Muslim municipality in administrative terms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true. Five days later they never mentioned any municipality whatsoever. They issued a purely military ultimatum. The president of the SDS was there with us at this meeting. Beco was pleading with them and asking for any kind of peaceful solution and that was resolutely rejected and what we had before us was an ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me to finish. This was only four or five days before this meeting. There was not a single incident that occurred between this meeting and the meeting when this ultimatum was issued to us, and this is a fact and, Your Honours, and I'm telling you all of this because it is a fact.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers will have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, just a second. Very well. Please continue. Put a pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me, but in -- it seems to me in terms of any issue about the dates of the meeting, apart from the fact that they appear to go -- be entered chronologically, it seems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I noted --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 6th of May appeared, 6th of June appeared, and then 6th of May appeared again and after which we see the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right, and we also see in the text of the meeting that's headed 6 June a reference to a dead-line of May 8th and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear in the [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- witness's evidence. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is what the gentleman says Mr. Husein. [In English] [As read] "We must not say that we are founding a temporary municipality because someone will betray us. They will not accept that and will prevent us from doing it. One of the options is to set up a municipality consisting of five MZ," local communities. "If the negotiations result in the decision that Prijedor should be part of a Serbian area, we will accept that but we will not live at gunpoint." [Interpretation] And then you also knew that Alija Izetbegovic could sign a document stating that Prijedor will remain in the Serb canton?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How did you jump to Alija Izetbegovic all of a sudden from Kozarac? This is a meeting that was held only four or five days before the meeting with the SDS. We had intended and wished to talk to the SDS in terms of how the problems could be resolved, but the SDS that held all power in their hands then refused any kind of discussion. They were only issuing an ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Take it slowly. Let us see what this Beco says. He wants a municipality of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no voting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says, "My own vote goes to" -- [In English] "My own vote goes to a municipality of Kozarac."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page now. Let us see the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [As read] "Conclusion. [In English] A civil municipality of Kozarac should be set up. It would be temporary in nature and all MZ," local communities, "should be able to join if they should so wish. "The Kamicani and Trnopolje" local communities "would rather not take a position until the local community assemblies have their say."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, don't you see that this is being done very seriously and that five local communes and Kozarac as the sixth one could have been a big Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said, "Do you see that serious work is being done on that"? No, I do not see any kind of serious work being done on that. What we see from the minutes is that this is being discussed. It's one thing if you are discussing something and it is a completely different matter if we are actually working on something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I read the conclusion, sir, the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it say that? Let me read it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The previous page, conclusion. [In English] [As read] "Conclusion: A civil municipality of Kozarac should be set up. It would be temporary in nature and all local communities should be able to join it if they should so wish."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's show the B/C/S version to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's right there, it's written there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where, where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Above the date on the left-hand side, above the date, the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, ah-ha, conclusion. Is this what you mean, to raise readiness as much as possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, I have something different in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Jasim Fazlic, Sejmenovic, see, you're speaking here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Previous page, go back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
