utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see this. Where are these conclusions stating that a municipality should be established? Of course that was not done and no concrete work started on that. However, I would be interested in seeing where it is that the gentleman sees that written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here it is, conclusion, to establish a civic municipality of Kozarac which would be of a temporary nature and all other local communes that wish could be asked to join them. And then the Kamicani and Trnopolje local communes would not take a position until the assemblies have their say, the commission for negotiations would be Kemo Fazlic, Ilkan Memic, and Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has nothing to do with the municipality. This negotiation has nothing to do with the municipality. Some of the attendees of this meeting obviously stated their intention to have a municipality established, but not a single step was taken in that direction, not a single step whatsoever. Your Honours, you will all agree that the establishment of a municipality is a long-term and demanding project.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but you, sir, were the one who procrastinated; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And you, sir, simultaneously with other representatives of the authorities were getting closer to a reported resolution at the international level and those of us on the ground who were fearing for our lives were waiting and listening to the radio and watching our TVs and waiting for the news so that we could allow ourselves a hope that everything would be resolved peacefully and that we would live normally as we used to. The negotiations at the international level were ongoing and of course our big hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, just a second. I wanted to make sure that we are on the correct page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Jasim Fazlic and after his response follows the conclusion, z-a-k-l-j-u-c-a-k. It's rather illegible but one can see it anyway. Can we please see the 8th of May? That means moving forward a few pages. Can we also find the Serbian version. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I saw 7th of May but where do we see 7th of May in English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't found it in translation. No, the meetings were held on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right, Mr. Sejmenovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not attend them on a daily basis. I attended perhaps two or three of these meetings, so I am somewhat competent to talk about the ones I did attend. As for the ones I didn't attend, I can give you my opinion on the basis of the context and my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 8th you did attend; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you have to finish in three or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to note with regret that I cannot consider this witness as having been examined in cross-examination. We are talking about his words here, the whole activities that are taking to war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please, please, let me not repeat what I said earlier. It's totally unacceptable. Finish in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, you were present so can we please show the following page in Serbian to Mr. Sejmenovic. Please have a look at what Husein M. says here. It says: [As read] "If after Lisbon the Prijedor municipality should find itself in Krajina, not one of us will be against it. We'll go and in the end we'll sign. [In English] There is no reason for them to fight for it's because Izetbegovic may put his signature to a Serbian canton." [Interpretation] A bit further down: [In English] "We will accept the decision made in Lisbon ... there is no threat of genocide to anyone here. Try to arrange a meeting at any cost with Zupljanin and Radic." [Interpretation] And then you say: "[In English] Some regions will be resolved by agreement. There will be an ..." [Interpretation] Now it's hard to read. Maybe you can help us. At the bottom here it says "some regions will ..."

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "... will be resolved by agreement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: By agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the following page in Serbian. And in English did we get it in Serbian? Can we please see the next page in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please read what you said after this. "We shall not surrender our weapons" --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the last sentence. "There are no guarantees to the people from their authorities," and that was the truth. We did opt for negotiations and new resolutions, but a few days later you prevented that with cannons and tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says here in the conclusion that tonight alert something and then I see here in English it's only translated that on Monday they would go to Banja Luka to have a meeting with representatives of Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because with you, with the SDS in Prijedor, it was not possible to talk any longer. So we had some hopes that your representatives in the Bosnian Krajina, that is to say in Banja Luka, would be more rational, would listen to us and come and see for themselves that we did not pose any threat and then we could go from there and try to seek a solution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the following two pages in English. One page further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that Nagib says: [In English] "Has a municipality been formally established in Ljubija? "No, but a police station has." [Interpretation] Do you know that Cehajic moved to the left bank and began working on establishing a municipality in Ljubija and that the police station there was taken over, as you can see from this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in that Ljubija it was not possible to establish a municipality. This is a hypothetical question which borders or is contrary to reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I was just noticing that of course the English and B/C/S pages don't respond -- do not correspond, so the witness -- if our attention is being drawn to something in the English, then I presume it should be on screen available to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be the following page in English -- rather, the following page in Serbian. That's citation of what Nagib said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After all these negotiations and political activities, Mr. Sejmenovic, what followed was Hambarine and the killing of soldiers in a car. And then what followed after that were other killings. Do you know that a Serbian policeman was killed from behind and then his relative killed four Muslims as an act of revenge? Are you familiar of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you interpret these facts without proper arguments because it was never established what exactly this was that happened down there. The non-Serbs were accused of a man fleeing to a Muslim-populated village after he killed this policeman and that the village was hiding the killer. That was what one could hear in public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document admitted and can we see another document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This should be your last question, Mr. Karadzic. While we admit this but if the parties, Mr. Robinson and the Prosecution, could take a look into the order of this, the way it is compiled or filed. I see some uncertain parts in terms of order. Yes, this will be admitted as Exhibit D1831. And, Mr. Karadzic, your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4593, please. I believe that there is a translation but let me read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [As read] "The situation is difficult. The lines are down. In Prijedor yesterday a reserve policeman of Serb ethnicity was killed from behind. Immediately after that a relative of the deceased killed four Muslims. The 3rd of May 1992." Was that the atmosphere in Prijedor, Mr. Sejmenovic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on the 3rd of May, 1992, all lines were in the hands of the Serbian authorities, the military and the police. Non-Serbs, the Bosniaks, did not have any lines, so how could they cut down your lines if they didn't have their own? I don't know who Milos is or why Milos wrote this, to whom he sent it, to whom did this paper arrive from. I'm talking about the facts concerning the 3rd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was about yesterday, the 2nd of May, the previous day. Was a Serbian policeman killed on the 2nd of May and then on the third of May or immediately on the 2nd of May, his relative killed four Muslims probably from behind?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this piece of news on the radio but I heard an interpretation of the Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And was a curfew imposed after this?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that curfew had been imposed. I'm not sure if it was imposed before or after this because after the 30th of April I did not go to Prijedor any longer so I cannot personally say what was the date on which the curfew was imposed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please just one more question, political in nature, because Mr. Sejmenovic was a deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will now tell you about a thesis that there were two authentic Muslim proposals and that we accepted both. The first proposal was the one coming from Mr. Izetbegovic, who was the first to mention and propose a division of Bosnia, that Bosnia should be independent, divided into three units. The other proposal came from Mr. Zulfikarpasic, that Bosnia should be unitary but that it should remain within Yugoslavia, and the Serbs accepted both. Silajdzic came out with a combination: Bosnia independent but unitary. That was something that we did not accept; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are just excerpts from events which are a speculation of yours at the moment. Throughout this time only you who had proposals or received proposals had power that you could use, extremely mighty power, and from this position with the power behind your back you offered, you accepted certain options or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did we accept that Bosnia should be independent with three units or that it should remain within Yugoslavia but be unitary and that we should give up on regionalisation?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details of your consultations and negotiations. I know officially what happened in general terms at some conferences, but I'm not fully competent to discuss that level of issues and problems.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for allowing me to ask this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that the question was not -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you think about admitting 1D4593?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, again, that depends to some extent on previous -- there's a smallish, thin, basis on the -- that is, I understand the question is asked because the answer of the witness does not necessarily give rise to admission. I appreciate that this may therefore be tendered by way of challenging the witness. That depends on the nature of the document. Since these documents have been admitted in the past in the court there have been several of these documents admitted and the Court decided it is going to assess -- allocate whatever weight it deems fit, it seems, I guess, to fall within the context of those earlier decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber considers there's some basis among the witness's evidence upon which we can admit this. This will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1832, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have re-examination, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It depends, actually, on the position taken by the Defence in connection with the one item I have in mind. At page 14 the Court and the Defence will recall there was a discussion about a document and the issue arose about which census it was connected with, the document related to the 1990 election and then finally the witness pointed out that in his view it related to an earlier census. If there's no objection to the admission of 00242E out of the book on the census regarding Prijedor, then I won't have to put it to the witness. If Defence wants me to do so, I can go through the formalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to defer to Dr. Karadzic on that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the essence is that the witness accepted that it wasn't 20 years but rather nine years, so that happened in 1981, the census was conducted then, it was in 1981. So if there is any dispute about that -- I'm trying to see what the point is. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Fine, apparently there's no agreement on that so let me just call up, in that case, 00242E and ask that it be shown to the witness. And if we could just highlight the numbers up above the graphic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, this is taken from the book, a much larger book on the census and portion related to Prijedor, which reflects a population in 1991 of 49.351 Muslims, 47.581 Serbs, and then a little over 6.000 Croats, et cetera. Does this conform to your understanding of what the 1991 census revealed and what the population figures were in Prijedor at that time?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may just say, this was not in dispute, though this census was never accepted, but rather the decision in 1990 was made with regard to the census that was conducted in 1981.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I now heard a sentence that this census was never accepted which is not true in the least. The census was accepted. The results were published in the Official Gazette of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Some political factors did not agree with the census because of their internal plans or reasons, but that is an issue that is outside the institutions. From the institutional point of view, both de facto and de jure, it is a valid, internationally approved census of the population, or rather, the results of the census of the population in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at which parliament session was that accepted, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's only valid once it goes through the parliamentary procedure and this didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's part of his -- it can be part of your submission in later -- your Defence case. Very well, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3701, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Sejmenovic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Robinson, the Defence motion to admit a public redacted version of Exhibit D1523 is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I have a quick clarifying question about your supplementary submission in relation to von Bezold subpoena. Do we have to discuss it in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, it's all public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you didn't provide the underlying material, we cannot confirm whether that was actually served to Mr. von Bezold and whether -- and also -- let me put it this way: Did you receive a correspondence in writing from the German government?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I received an e-mail, Mr. President, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you didn't provide us with that e-mail?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I didn't but I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know the contact details of Mr. von Bezold?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, the German government has declined to provide us with that. They preferred to be the intermediary to serve the document on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll rise for today and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we need to give a separate number for that Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D1832, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson, did you have anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually I did, Mr. President. We want to withdraw the 62nd motion for disclosure violation because the Prosecution has called to our attention that the document that was the subject of that motion had earlier been disclosed to us so we have no reason to ask anyone to continue to work on that and we withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume on Monday at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 31st day of October, 2011, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
